meta.about: Amara Raja Batteries Limited [1] (ARBL), the flagship company of the Amara Raja Group, is the technology leader and is one of the largest manufacturers of lead-acid batteries for both industrial and automotive applications in the Indian storage battery industry. ARBL has prestigious OEMs as its clients. The Company's Industrial and Automotive batteries are exported to over 50 countries across the globe. In India, Amara Raja is the preferred supplier to major telecom service providers, Telecom equipment manufacturers, UPS sector (OEM & Replacement), Indian Railways and to Power, Oil & Gas among other industry segments. Termination of Shareholders Agreement (tie up) with Johnson Control [2]

assumptions._note: Standalone model (Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Ltd = the lead-acid business, lubes and a little lithium trading), the basis the street uses for the core (MOFSL, Nuvama, Anand Rathi, 360 ONE, ICICI Direct and Avendus value standalone FY28E EPS). FY26 base = Screener standalone (revenue Rs13,549 cr, EBITDA Rs1,551 cr, PAT Rs970 cr incl. Rs259 cr net exceptional income). One segment ('core') so that bull/bear deltas flow through the engine's SOTP scenarios. segments.name: Lead-acid batteries and allied products (standalone Amara Raja)
segments._why: Revenue = sum of three business lines (assumptions.build, checked in ARE&M.ctx.js). FY27E +14.6%: Q1FY27 +20.6% (OEM 4W +24%, 2W +35%, aftermarket ~+15%, home energy +60%), price increases of ~3% in June and 2-3% in August, a normal Q2 base (Q2FY26 +8%), then the post-GST OEM base from Q3; automotive exports (−20% in Q1) and telecom lead-acid stay weak; lithium pack trading moves to ARACT from Q2. FY28-29E ~9%: management's 9-10% medium-term volume growth for lead-acid (Q1FY27 call), replacement demand from the FY26-27 OEM surge, exports recovering, industrial ex-telecom (UPS, data centres) growing. Street FY27E: MOFSL Rs15,526 cr, Nuvama Rs15,628 cr, Anand Rathi Rs15,409 cr, 360 ONE Rs15,975 cr.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener standalone basis): FY24 14.4%, FY25 13.2%, FY26 11.4%, Q1FY27 10.1% (−140bp YoY: ~0.9pp strategic spending on brand, the Amaron Assist pilot and debottlenecking, plus alloy, sulphuric acid and plastics costs, warranty provisions and freight). FY27E 10.8%: price increases of ~3% (June) and 2-3% (August) catch up with costs, B2B with a lag; strategic spending normalises 'over the next couple of quarters'; traded tubular batteries fall as the own plant meets demand. FY28-29E 11.6-12.0%: operating leverage on ~9% growth and less trading; below management's 13-14% aim, which has no date. Street FY27/28E: MOFSL 10.7/11.8%, Nuvama 11.3/11.5%, Anand Rathi 10.7/12.1%, 360 ONE 11.5/12.9%.

assumptions._capexWhy: Lead-acid capex: ~Rs400 cr in FY27 (of the ~Rs1,700 cr group plan, ~Rs1,300 cr is New Energy in ARACT; Q1FY27 call); FY26 ~Rs600 cr gross, ~Rs500 cr net of insurance (Q4FY26 call). FY28-29E Rs450-500 cr: debottlenecking 4W/2W capacity ('more throughput in the same four walls') and the tubular plant. ARACT capex is funded by equity infusions (build.aract.infusion), not here.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs548 cr; Q1FY27 Rs140 cr (run-rate ~Rs560 cr). The rate on average gross block is set so FY27E depreciation is ~Rs570 cr. CWIP is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero: the engine's 'treasury' includes the investments in subsidiaries at cost (ARACT, ARCSPL, ARPSL: Rs2,234 cr at Mar-26), which earn no interest. Interest on liquid funds and on borrowings is built in ARE&M.ctx.js and written into otherIncome and interest.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built (ARE&M.ctx.js checks it): foreign-exchange gains Rs30 cr (FY26 Rs42.8 cr, FY25 Rs38.2 cr; exports ~12% of revenue, not forecast at the FY26 level) + scrap sales Rs12 cr (FY26 Rs12.5 cr) + interest on the Rs120 cr loans to ARPSL and other deposits Rs9 cr (FY26 Rs4.0 cr, loans given during FY26) + other items Rs22 cr (FY26 Rs28.6 cr incl. write-backs) + 7% on positive net liquid funds after ARACT infusions. FY26 normal other income Rs91.9 cr (AR FY26 note 23, before Rs259 cr exceptional income that Screener adds to other income); TTM to Jun-2026 Rs88 cr (Screener 'other income normal'); FY27E is lower because mutual-fund gains (Rs8 cr) go with the cash and FX gains are not assumed to repeat in full.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (warranty unwinding, leases, working-capital debt)
assumptions._interestWhy: Built: unwinding of discount on warranty provisions Rs17 cr + lease interest Rs10 cr (FY26 Rs16.8 + 10.0 cr, AR FY26 note 26) + 7.5% on average net borrowings (FY26 'others' Rs13.9 cr on average borrowings of ~Rs210 cr). The parent had net debt of Rs156 cr at Mar-26 (borrowings Rs271 cr, cash Rs115 cr) and borrows to fund ARACT in FY27.
assumptions._taxWhy: New regime (25.17%) plus disallowances: FY26 effective ~25.8%, Q1FY27 25.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS Rs10.6 for FY26 = 20% of EPS (Rs194 cr); 20% in FY24-26 (Screener; AR FY26).

build._why: Automotive (OEM Rs1,800 cr + aftermarket, home energy and auto exports Rs8,399 cr in FY26, Nuvama): Q1FY27 domestic auto +20%+, home energy +60%, exports −20%; H2 against the post-GST OEM base. Industrial (Rs3,018 cr: telecom, UPS and data centres, railways, power, solar, industrial exports): +2% in Q1FY27 as UPS (+10% volume) offsets telecom moving to lithium; Nuvama models +2%/+4%. Others (Rs332 cr: lubes Rs205.5 cr, services, export incentives and scrap): lubes ~Rs50 cr a quarter and growing.

aract._infusionWhy: FY27E: brings the investment in ARACT from Rs1,500 cr (Mar-26) to the ~Rs2,500 cr 'initial risk capital' management says completes the five facilities (Q1FY27 call); Rs400 cr was already in by Aug-2026. FY28-29E: none in the core cash path; further cell capacity is not approved and is excluded (a risk, see the report).
aract._lossWhy: GAM estimates (no company guidance; brokers publish only NPVs). FY26 ARACT loss Rs73 cr (Rs98 cr before tax; AOC-1) on Rs787 cr of pack revenue; consolidated less standalone profit −Rs12 cr in Q1FY27. FY27E: cell R&D of Rs100-150 cr (Q1FY27 call), BESS start-up from Q3FY27 (5-8% operating margin guided). FY28E: the 2 GWh cell line starts (Q2-CY2027) with depreciation and low utilisation. FY29E: BESS at ~5 GWh and better cell utilisation narrow the loss; breakeven FY30E. Bull: BESS ramps fast, breakeven FY30E with smaller losses. Bear: cell approvals lag, breakeven only after FY30E.

dcf._betaWhy: Lead-acid battery maker with near-zero leverage and lead-price pass-through: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5% (same as Exide).
dcf._tgWhy: Batteries track the vehicle parc, power back-up and industrial capex: ~5.5% nominal long-run growth (house range 5-6%), below nominal GDP as telecom, e-rickshaw and EV traction move to lithium.
dcf._fadeWhy: Growth fades from ~9% to 7%; margin 12.5% (between FY26's 11.4% and management's 13-14% aim); capex 3.5% of sales (FY27-29E 2.6-2.7% plus periodic capacity steps); depreciation 3.3% of sales (FY26 4.0%).
dcf._netCashWhy: The engine adds 'treasury' at FY27E: net liquid funds plus the investments in subsidiaries at cost. So the DCF is a core DCF plus ARACT and the other subsidiaries at cost, a cross-check only.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: OEM demand and the replacement wave keep lead-acid volumes growing double digit, price increases stick and trading falls, so margin reaches ~12.5% by FY29E; ARACT's BESS plant fills fast and losses shrink (breakeven FY30E).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Auto-OEM growth reverses against the post-GST base, alloy, acid and plastic costs outrun prices (margin ~11%), exports stay weak and telecom moves to lithium faster; ARACT's cells are not approved on time, losses last beyond FY30E and the market values the subsidiary at half of book.

cover.headline: India's number-two battery maker, priced for disappointment at ₹755
cover.lead: Amara Raja (Amaron) is half of India's lead-acid battery duopoly with Exide: car and two-wheeler batteries for OEMs and the replacement market, home-energy and industrial batteries, and the leader in telecom. Q1FY27 revenue grew 20.6% but the EBITDA margin fell to 10.1%, and the stock then fell ~22% in seven weeks. Around the core sits ARACT, a lithium subsidiary with ₹1,900 cr of equity, a pack business, a BESS plant and a cell plant due in 2027. The street values Amara Raja **in parts**, and so do we: the core at **14x Sep-28E standalone EPS of ₹63.0 (₹881)** + ARACT at book less the present value of losses to breakeven (₹115) + other subsidiaries at book (₹38) = **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: P/E on all standalone EPS ₹944, DCF ₹1,207. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: OEM volumes grew 24% (cars) and 35% (two-wheelers) in Q1FY27 after the GST cut, aftermarket ~15% and home energy 60%; those OEM batteries come back as replacement demand in 3-4 years. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct0}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct0}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct0}} and EBITDA margin {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} → {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}.

arguments.h: But margins are the problem, and an honest one
arguments.p: The EBITDA margin was 16-18% a decade ago, 14.4% in FY24, 11.4% in FY26 and 10.1% in Q1FY27: alloys, acid and plastics, more traded goods, OEM mix and spending on brand and capacity. EPS before one-offs grew only ~2% a year in FY21-26. Management still aims for 13-14% but gives no date; we assume 12% by FY29E.

arguments.h: Lithium: a cheaper bet than Exide's, still a cost
arguments.p: ARACT has ₹1,900 cr of equity (Exide has put ₹4,902 cr into its plant), ₹787 cr of pack revenue and a ₹73 cr loss. The cell plant has slipped to 2027, its Chinese partner fell away and 16 GWh is now an "ambition". We value ARACT at book less ₹171 cr of losses still to come (₹115 a share), in line with MOFSL and ICICI Direct, below Nuvama and Anand Rathi.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price has done the work
arguments.p: At ₹755 the stock trades at 13.2x our FY28E EPS. Net of the subsidiaries (~₹137 a share), the core trades at 9.8x Sep-28E EPS against a 15.2x median since 2021; auto-component stocks sat 7.8% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026, and our 14x includes that. The post-Q1 street median target is ₹1,075.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether the June and August price increases lift the margin back above 10.5%, and how much trading falls.
BESS plant start (guided for Q3FY27) and its first orders; ARACT's losses in the consolidated accounts.
Equipment for the 2 GWh NMC line (due Q3FY27), cell samples to OEMs, and the re-opened 10 GWh PLI tender.
Any decision on lithium funding beyond the ~₹2,500 cr of initial risk capital.
Export recovery in the Middle East; lead, alloy, acid and plastic prices.

sections.title: Amaron, PowerZone and telecom back-up: India's number-two battery maker, with a lithium arm on the side

blocks.p: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility (Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh; incorporated 1985; renamed from Amara Raja Batteries in 2023) makes lead-acid batteries in 15 facilities around Tirupati and Chittoor: ~70 mn automotive units and ~2.4 bn Ah of industrial capacity a year, plus a tubular plant. It sells under Amaron (cars, two-wheelers), PowerZone and Quanta (industrial), through 1,500+ direct partners and 1,00,000+ points of sale, and exports to 70+ countries (₹1,653 cr, 12% of FY26 revenue). About three-quarters of revenue is automotive (OEM and replacement) and home energy; a fifth is industrial, where it leads telecom. ₹2,128 cr of FY26 revenue (16%) was traded goods: inverters, home UPS, lubes and batteries bought from others when its own plants were full. The New Energy business (lithium packs, chargers, a cell giga-factory and a BESS plant under construction in Telangana) sits in the 100% subsidiary **ARACT**; lead recycling sits in **ARCSPL** (Cheyyar, Tamil Nadu).

sections.title: A two-player lead-acid market enjoying a post-GST vehicle boom while lithium takes telecom and e-rickshaws

blocks.p: Organised Indian lead-acid batteries are a two-player market: Exide (FY26 standalone revenue ₹17,269 cr) and Amara Raja (₹13,549 cr) supply most car and two-wheeler OEMs and lead the replacement market; Amara Raja leads telecom (>60% share across lead and lithium, Q1FY27 call) and Exide leads most other industrial lines. Both now also sell lithium-ion packs and are building cell plants. Demand comes from new vehicles (OEM), the replacement cycle (a car battery lasts ~3-4 years), home energy (inverters, tubular batteries), industrial back-up (UPS, data centres, railways, power, solar) and exports. Auto OEM volumes jumped after the September-2025 GST cut (Amara Raja's 4W OEM +24%, 2W +35% in Q1FY27); management sees the lead-acid market growing ~9-10% a year in volume over the medium term (Q1FY27 call).

**Our read:** lead-acid is in a good phase (an OEM boom that feeds a replacement wave, strong home energy, data-centre UPS), but it is a mature, cost-pass-through market with one strong rival. Lithium is not a near-term threat to car starter batteries, but it has already taken much of telecom, where Amara Raja was strongest, and it will take EV traction batteries.

bullets: **The tailwind reaches Amara Raja's volumes.** OEM volumes grew faster than the industry in Q1FY27, home energy took share in a strong summer, and the bigger car and two-wheeler parc will feed replacement demand later.

**It has not reached margins.** Alloys, sulphuric acid and plastics rose faster than prices; B2B (OEM) prices follow with a lag; more of the growth came from traded tubular batteries and OEM supplies, both lower-margin; and management chose to spend on brand (IPL), the Amaron Assist pilot and debottlenecking. Margin fell from 11.5% to 10.1% YoY in Q1FY27 while revenue grew 21%.

**The lithium transition cuts against it at the edges.** Telecom lead-acid, e-rickshaws and future EV traction are where lead-acid loses; Amara Raja is replacing telecom lead-acid with its own lithium packs (combined telecom share >60%), but those packs sit in ARACT and earn little.

blocks.p: **Margin.** EBITDA margin (Screener standalone basis): FY24 14.4%, FY25 13.2%, FY26 11.4%, Q1FY27 10.1% (−140bp YoY: ~0.9pp strategic spending on brand, the Amaron Assist pilot and debottlenecking, plus alloy, sulphuric acid and plastics costs, warranty provisions and freight). FY27E 10.8%: price increases of ~3% (June) and 2-3% (August) catch up with costs, B2B with a lag; strategic spending normalises 'over the next couple of quarters'; traded tubular batteries fall as the own plant meets demand. FY28-29E 11.6-12.0%: operating leverage on ~9% growth and less trading; below management's 13-14% aim, which has no date. Street FY27/28E: MOFSL 10.7/11.8%, Nuvama 11.3/11.5%, Anand Rathi 10.7/12.1%, 360 ONE 11.5/12.9%. Gross margin (after materials and traded goods) fell from 32.2% in FY25 to 30.9% in FY26 and ~28.5% in Q1FY27 (360 ONE; MOFSL: raw materials 71.5% of sales). Each 0.5 point of margin is ~₹3.5 of FY28E EPS (~6%).

blocks.callout: **So what:** the core is a reliable grower, not a margin story: ~9-15% revenue growth, an ~11-12% margin, capex of ~₹400-500 cr a year and EPS before one-offs rising from ₹42 (FY26) to ₹{{F.eps.2|n1}} (FY29E), helped by operating leverage and, once the ARACT funding stops, interest on rebuilt cash. Management's 13-14% margin would add ~15% to our FY29E EPS; we do not assume it.

sections.title: ARACT: ₹1,900 cr invested, a pack business that sells and a cell plant still to come: worth ~₹115 a share to us

blocks.p: Giga Cell plant at Divitipally: phase 1 = 2 GWh NMC (cylindrical 2170 cells), equipment due in Q3FY27, operations from Q2-CY2027 (commercialisation in H1FY28); 16 GWh by FY30 was the original plan (₹9,500 cr over ~10 years) and is now 'a long-term ambition' to be calibrated to demand, with ESS (LFP) cells possibly prioritised. Customer Qualification Plant inaugurated 15-Jul-2026; E-Positive research lab to start in Q2FY27. 10 GWh BESS assembly plant (LFP, imported 314 Ah cells): initial capex ₹250-300 cr, operations in Q3FY27, ~5 GWh utilisation within 6-7 months, operating margin 5-6% at first, 7-8% with localisation. Pack business: telecom and 3W/2W packs, revenue ₹809 cr in FY26 (NEB segment), ₹209 cr in Q1FY27 (+70%). Initial risk capital agreed ~₹2,500 cr to complete five facilities (cell plant phase 1, CQP, E-Positive lab, BESS, packs); later capacity to be funded by the holding company and/or other options; ₹700-800 cr a year of post-tax, post-dividend cash generation at the parent (Q1FY27 call). FY27 group capex ~₹1,700 cr, of which ~₹1,300 cr New Energy; ₹450 cr spent in Q1 (Q1FY27 call).

sections.title: Competitive advantage: a strong number-two franchise, but no pricing power and no edge in lithium cells

verdicts: Amaron is the second-best-known battery brand in India, with 1,500+ direct partners and 1,00,000+ points of sale; a D2C service pilot (Amaron Assist) started in Q1FY27 (Q1FY27 deck).
The replacement buyer chooses by brand and availability; Amaron is one of two national brands.

~70 mn automotive units a year; own lead recycling at Cheyyar (100,000 t refining capacity, ~88% of lead from recycled sources, but scrap prices currently make recycled lead cost the same as LME lead: Q1FY27 call).
Captive recycling secures lead and EPR compliance but adds no cost edge while scrap is dear.
Supplies most 2W and 4W OEMs; OEM volumes +24% (4W) and +35% (2W) in Q1FY27; >60% of telecom across lead and lithium.
Sticky and growing, but OEM and telecom business is priced on lead formulas with thin margins.
EBITDA margin 15-17% in FY15-21, 14-15% in FY23-24, 11.4% in FY26 and 10.1% in Q1FY27 (Screener standalone): input costs are passed on late; traded goods now ~16% of revenue at lower margins.
A duopoly that competes; costs are passed on late, not marked up.
Own NMC cell (2170) from earlier technology access, no current partner; cathode from China; cells 15-20% dearer than imports; not in the ACC PLI scheme so far.
No advantage yet; the edge is customers (telecom, 3W) and the pack business.

sections.title: Revenue tripled in ten years, but the EBITDA margin fell from 16-18% to 11%: a premium battery maker that became an ordinary one

blocks.p: Standalone revenue (the lead-acid business) was ₹4,618 cr in FY16 and ₹13,549 cr in FY26: 11.4% a year, and 13.6% a year since FY21. Growth came from volumes (cars, two-wheelers, inverters, telecom), from passing on lead costs, and since FY24 from more traded goods (₹2,128 cr, 16% of FY26 revenue: inverters, home UPS, lubes and batteries bought in). The weak spot is margin: 16-18% in FY15-17 and 14-16% to FY21, then 11.8% in FY22, a recovery to 14.4% in FY24 and a slide to 11.4% in FY26 and 10.1% in Q1FY27 as alloys, acid and plastics rose, trading grew and the company spent on brand and capacity. Reported profit carries one-offs: a ₹48 cr fire charge in FY23 and insurance income of ₹111 cr (FY25) and ₹259 cr net (FY26). Before them, EPS went from ₹37.9 (FY21) to ₹42.4 (FY26): just 2% a year.

sections.title: Where the cash went: ₹6,420 cr of operating cash in six years, ₹2,233 cr of it into subsidiaries

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 the standalone business generated ₹6,420 cr of operating cash. It spent ₹3,672 cr on lead-acid capex (₹440-760 cr a year, including reinstating the Chittoor tubular plant after the January-2023 fire), paid ₹835 cr of dividends (20% payout since FY24) and put ₹2,233 cr of equity into subsidiaries: ARACT (lithium-ion) ₹1,500 cr, ARCSPL (lead recycling) ₹600 cr and ARPSL (chargers, power systems) ₹133 cr, plus ₹120 cr of loans to ARPSL. A further ₹400 cr went into ARACT by Aug-2026 (₹1,900 cr in total). Management's group capex for FY27 is ~₹1,700 cr, of which ~₹1,300 cr is New Energy; it calls ~₹2,500 cr the "initial risk capital" for lithium and says the parent can fund it from ₹700-800 cr a year of cash after tax and dividends.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** lead-acid needs modest capital (capex ~4-5% of revenue) and turns cash; lithium needs a lot more (the original plan was ₹9,500 cr for 16 GWh). So far Amara Raja has been more cautious than Exide (₹1,900 cr into ARACT vs Exide's ₹4,902 cr into its cell company) and has built a pack business that already sells ₹800 cr a year. But the cell plant has slipped to 2027, the Chinese technology partner fell away, and management now calls 16 GWh an "ambition". Every rupee beyond the ₹2,500 cr of risk capital is still undecided.

sections.title: Earnings quality: cash-backed, but read FY25-26 profit before insurance income

bullets: **Cash conversion is good.** Cash from operations was ₹1,340 cr in FY26 (138% of reported profit, 86% of EBITDA) and ₹1,375 cr in FY25 (143% of profit).

**One-offs are labelled but large.** FY26 PBT includes ₹259 cr of net exceptional income (insurance ₹303 cr less a ₹43.8 cr labour-code charge): 20% of PBT. FY25 includes ₹111 cr of insurance; FY23 a ₹47.65 cr fire charge. Screener adds these to other income. We value on EPS before them (FY26 ₹42.4, not ₹53.0).

**Other income is small and mostly operating.** FY26 ₹91.9 cr before exceptional items (company): foreign-exchange gains ₹42.8 cr, scrap ₹12.5 cr, mutual-fund gains ₹8.1 cr, interest ₹4.0 cr, other ₹24.7 cr. We forecast ₹73 cr for FY27E (TTM ₹88 cr): the cash is gone and we do not assume FY26's FX gain repeats in full.

**Where the judgement sits:** warranty provisions (raised in Q1FY27 as product costs rose; their unwinding is ₹17 cr of finance cost); goodwill of ₹428 cr from the Mangal demerger, tested annually; the investments in subsidiaries carried at cost (₹2,234 cr) while ARACT's own book value is ₹1,431 cr; debottlenecking costs expensed, not capitalised (Q1FY27 call).
**Related parties:** ARCSPL sells recycled lead to the company; ARPSL owes ₹120 cr; Mangal Industries (promoter group) was the plastics supplier before its battery-components business was folded in.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN** for the standalone company (joint auditors Price Waterhouse and K.S. Rao & Co, unmodified opinions; exceptional items clearly shown). Investors should still read the consolidated accounts: consolidated profit was ₹74 cr below standalone in FY26 and that gap will widen while the cell plant starts.

sections.title: Nearly debt-free, but no longer cash-rich: ₹2,234 cr sits in subsidiaries and the parent borrows a little

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 the standalone company had ₹271 cr of short-term borrowings and ₹101 cr of lease liabilities against ₹115 cr of cash: a small net debt of ~₹156 cr (before leases). Its ₹2,585 cr of investments were almost all subsidiaries at cost: ARACT ₹1,500 cr, ARCSPL ₹600 cr, ARPSL ₹133 cr; mutual funds had been run down from ₹62 cr to nil. Goodwill of ₹428 cr comes from the Mangal plastics demerger. Working capital is moderate: on Screener's basis inventory was 89 days, receivables 31 days and payables 47 days in FY26, a 74-day cash cycle (93 days in FY21-22). In our model the parent borrows ~₹500 cr in FY27 to put ₹1,000 cr into ARACT, and turns net cash again in FY28 if no more lithium money is needed.

sections.title: The street after Q1: one Buy, five Hold/Neutral; median target ₹1,075

blocks.p: Six houses updated after the Q1FY27 results (10-Aug-2026): Buy from Nuvama (₹1,130); Hold or Neutral from 360 ONE (₹1,195), Anand Rathi (₹1,080), J.P. Morgan (₹1,070), Nomura (₹1,048) and Motilal Oswal (₹944). The median target is ₹1,075, +42% above the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹755. But those targets were set with the stock at ~₹970; it then fell ~22% to ₹755 by 30-Sep-2026 (Exide fell ~13% from mid-August) without any change in ratings that we could find. Four of the six publish a method and all value **standalone FY28E EPS** at 12-18x; MOFSL, Nuvama and Anand Rathi add the New Energy business separately (₹92 to ₹356 a share). Before Q1, ICICI Direct (Hold, ₹960) and Avendus Spark (Add, ₹975) used the same structure. sections.title: Our honest summary: an ordinary-margin battery franchise at a below-average price, with a lithium option valued at cost; BUY

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's number-two lead-acid battery franchise (Amaron; OEM and telecom relationships; growing home energy), nearly debt-free and cash-generative, in a good volume cycle (post-GST OEM boom, a replacement wave to come, data-centre UPS). Margins have slid to ~10-11% and underlying EPS has barely grown in five years. Attached: ARACT, a lithium subsidiary with ₹1,900 cr of equity, a profitable-ish pack business, a cheap BESS line and a cell plant that will not produce until 2027.

**What you are paying:** ₹755 is 16.4x our FY27E and 13.2x FY28E standalone EPS. Net of the subsidiaries, the core trades at 9.8x Sep-28E EPS against a 15.2x median since 2021, while auto-component stocks were 7.8% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. Our sum of the parts gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): BUY. The street's median target (₹1,075) is higher still; it was set before the stock fell ~22% in seven weeks. We do not pay for BESS profits or a cell ramp; the upside is in the core.

assumptions._note: Standalone model (Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Ltd = the lead-acid business, lubes and a little lithium trading), the basis the street uses for the core (MOFSL, Nuvama, Anand Rathi, 360 ONE, ICICI Direct and Avendus value standalone FY28E EPS). The lithium-ion subsidiary ARACT and the other subsidiaries (ARCSPL recycling, ARPSL, ARBME) are valued separately in the sum of the parts. FY26 base = Screener standalone (revenue Rs13,549 cr, EBITDA Rs1,551 cr, PAT Rs970 cr incl. Rs259 cr net exceptional income). One segment ('core') so that bull/bear deltas flow through the engine's SOTP scenarios. Core and ARACT values are computed in tools/authoring/ARE&M.ctx.js and written here by ARE&M.val.js, which also writes the built other income and finance cost.

segments.name: Lead-acid batteries and allied products (standalone Amara Raja)
segments._why: Revenue = sum of three business lines (assumptions.build, checked in ARE&M.ctx.js). FY27E +14.6%: Q1FY27 +20.6% (OEM 4W +24%, 2W +35%, aftermarket ~+15%, home energy +60%), price increases of ~3% in June and 2-3% in August, a normal Q2 base (Q2FY26 +8%), then the post-GST OEM base from Q3; automotive exports (−20% in Q1) and telecom lead-acid stay weak; lithium pack trading moves to ARACT from Q2. FY28-29E ~9%: management's 9-10% medium-term volume growth for lead-acid (Q1FY27 call), replacement demand from the FY26-27 OEM surge, exports recovering, industrial ex-telecom (UPS, data centres) growing. Street FY27E: MOFSL Rs15,526 cr, Nuvama Rs15,628 cr, Anand Rathi Rs15,409 cr, 360 ONE Rs15,975 cr.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener standalone basis): FY24 14.4%, FY25 13.2%, FY26 11.4%, Q1FY27 10.1% (−140bp YoY: ~0.9pp strategic spending on brand, the Amaron Assist pilot and debottlenecking, plus alloy, sulphuric acid and plastics costs, warranty provisions and freight). FY27E 10.8%: price increases of ~3% (June) and 2-3% (August) catch up with costs, B2B with a lag; strategic spending normalises 'over the next couple of quarters'; traded tubular batteries fall as the own plant meets demand. FY28-29E 11.6-12.0%: operating leverage on ~9% growth and less trading; below management's 13-14% aim, which has no date. Street FY27/28E: MOFSL 10.7/11.8%, Nuvama 11.3/11.5%, Anand Rathi 10.7/12.1%, 360 ONE 11.5/12.9%.

assumptions._capexWhy: Lead-acid capex: ~Rs400 cr in FY27 (of the ~Rs1,700 cr group plan, ~Rs1,300 cr is New Energy in ARACT; Q1FY27 call); FY26 ~Rs600 cr gross, ~Rs500 cr net of insurance (Q4FY26 call). FY28-29E Rs450-500 cr: debottlenecking 4W/2W capacity ('more throughput in the same four walls') and the tubular plant. ARACT capex is funded by equity infusions (build.aract.infusion), not here.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs548 cr; Q1FY27 Rs140 cr (run-rate ~Rs560 cr). The rate on average gross block is set so FY27E depreciation is ~Rs570 cr. CWIP is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero: the engine's 'treasury' includes the investments in subsidiaries at cost (ARACT, ARCSPL, ARPSL: Rs2,234 cr at Mar-26), which earn no interest. Interest on liquid funds and on borrowings is built in ARE&M.ctx.js and written into otherIncome and interest.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built (ARE&M.ctx.js checks it): foreign-exchange gains Rs30 cr (FY26 Rs42.8 cr, FY25 Rs38.2 cr; exports ~12% of revenue, not forecast at the FY26 level) + scrap sales Rs12 cr (FY26 Rs12.5 cr) + interest on the Rs120 cr loans to ARPSL and other deposits Rs9 cr (FY26 Rs4.0 cr, loans given during FY26) + other items Rs22 cr (FY26 Rs28.6 cr incl. write-backs) + 7% on positive net liquid funds after ARACT infusions. FY26 normal other income Rs91.9 cr (AR FY26 note 23, before Rs259 cr exceptional income that Screener adds to other income); TTM to Jun-2026 Rs88 cr (Screener 'other income normal'); FY27E is lower because mutual-fund gains (Rs8 cr) go with the cash and FX gains are not assumed to repeat in full.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (warranty unwinding, leases, working-capital debt)
assumptions._interestWhy: Built: unwinding of discount on warranty provisions Rs17 cr + lease interest Rs10 cr (FY26 Rs16.8 + 10.0 cr, AR FY26 note 26) + 7.5% on average net borrowings (FY26 'others' Rs13.9 cr on average borrowings of ~Rs210 cr). The parent had net debt of Rs156 cr at Mar-26 (borrowings Rs271 cr, cash Rs115 cr) and borrows to fund ARACT in FY27.
assumptions._taxWhy: New regime (25.17%) plus disallowances: FY26 effective ~25.8%, Q1FY27 25.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS Rs10.6 for FY26 = 20% of EPS (Rs194 cr); 20% in FY24-26 (Screener; AR FY26).

build._why: Automotive (OEM Rs1,800 cr + aftermarket, home energy and auto exports Rs8,399 cr in FY26, Nuvama): Q1FY27 domestic auto +20%+, home energy +60%, exports −20%; H2 against the post-GST OEM base. Industrial (Rs3,018 cr: telecom, UPS and data centres, railways, power, solar, industrial exports): +2% in Q1FY27 as UPS (+10% volume) offsets telecom moving to lithium; Nuvama models +2%/+4%. Others (Rs332 cr: lubes Rs205.5 cr, services, export incentives and scrap): lubes ~Rs50 cr a quarter and growing.

aract._infusionWhy: FY27E: brings the investment in ARACT from Rs1,500 cr (Mar-26) to the ~Rs2,500 cr 'initial risk capital' management says completes the five facilities (Q1FY27 call); Rs400 cr was already in by Aug-2026. FY28-29E: none in the core cash path; further cell capacity is not approved and is excluded (a risk, see the report).
aract._lossWhy: GAM estimates (no company guidance; brokers publish only NPVs). FY26 ARACT loss Rs73 cr (Rs98 cr before tax; AOC-1) on Rs787 cr of pack revenue; consolidated less standalone profit −Rs12 cr in Q1FY27. FY27E: cell R&D of Rs100-150 cr (Q1FY27 call), BESS start-up from Q3FY27 (5-8% operating margin guided). FY28E: the 2 GWh cell line starts (Q2-CY2027) with depreciation and low utilisation. FY29E: BESS at ~5 GWh and better cell utilisation narrow the loss; breakeven FY30E. Bull: BESS ramps fast, breakeven FY30E with smaller losses. Bear: cell approvals lag, breakeven only after FY30E.

dcf._betaWhy: Lead-acid battery maker with near-zero leverage and lead-price pass-through: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5% (same as Exide).
dcf._tgWhy: Batteries track the vehicle parc, power back-up and industrial capex: ~5.5% nominal long-run growth (house range 5-6%), below nominal GDP as telecom, e-rickshaw and EV traction move to lithium.
dcf._fadeWhy: Growth fades from ~9% to 7%; margin 12.5% (between FY26's 11.4% and management's 13-14% aim); capex 3.5% of sales (FY27-29E 2.6-2.7% plus periodic capacity steps); depreciation 3.3% of sales (FY26 4.0%).
dcf._netCashWhy: The engine adds 'treasury' at FY27E: net liquid funds plus the investments in subsidiaries at cost. So the DCF is a core DCF plus ARACT and the other subsidiaries at cost, a cross-check only.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: OEM demand and the replacement wave keep lead-acid volumes growing double digit, price increases stick and trading falls, so margin reaches ~12.5% by FY29E; ARACT's BESS plant fills fast and losses shrink (breakeven FY30E).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Auto-OEM growth reverses against the post-GST base, alloy, acid and plastic costs outrun prices (margin ~11%), exports stay weak and telecom moves to lithium faster; ARACT's cells are not approved on time, losses last beyond FY30E and the market values the subsidiary at half of book.
